title: Comparison of corneal endothelial cell loss during manual small-incision cataract surgery using viscoelastic-assisted nucleus removal versus continuous balanced salt solution plus technique - Randomized controlled trial

indication: Cataract with nuclear sclerosis grade 1-5, with or without pseudoexfoliation (15/204), controlled diabetes (37/204) or hypertension (31/204); MSICS with rigid PMMA IOL; eyes below the ECD inclusion minimum, AC depth below 2.5 mm, hard mature or subluxated cataract and previous ocular surgery excluded

groups.description: MSICS with viscoelastic (2% HPMC)-assisted nucleus delivery (Group 1, OVD)
MSICS with continuous BSS-plus-assisted nucleus delivery (Group 2, BSS plus)

series.baseline_label: Preoperative ECD of the operated eye (SP-2000P specular microscope, manual count of 70 cells, mean of three readings)
series.notes: mean ± SD; columns follow the header order Preoperative G1/G2, 1 day G1/G2, 1 month (day 30) G1/G2; day 1 and day 30 converted from days

series.baseline_label: Preoperative ECD of the operated eye (SP-2000P specular microscope, manual count of 70 cells, mean of three readings)
series.notes: mean ± SD; columns follow the header order Preoperative G1/G2, 1 day G1/G2, 1 month (day 30) G1/G2; day 1 and day 30 converted from days

exclusions.reason: changes of the same series and p-values; the absolute ECD series is used

notes: Randomized controlled trial (computer-generated randomization, masked postoperative examiners), single surgeon, 204 patients (103 and 101).
The postoperative visits are day 1 and day 30 (Methods, abstract and caption); the Table 5b header says '1 month'. Day 30 is converted as 30 days.
The Table 5b row label reads 'Mean±SD (µm)', but the caption and Results identify the values as endothelial cell density.
Methods once name BSS plus for both groups; the surgical-technique paragraph and Table 1 assign HPMC viscoelastic to Group 1 and BSS plus to Group 2, which is used here.
Two standard MSICS nucleus-delivery techniques compared without an investigational agent; both are control.
